subject: Next steps: confirming decision owner & procurement path for Avatech
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: confirming decision owner & procurement path for Avatech

Hi Lina — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can get you a clean mutual action plan (MAP):

Recap from today's demo/discovery:
- Use case: embed Redwood inference for customer support triage + dynamic knowledge retrieval (expected 5M tokens/month initially).
- Key success criteria: sub-150ms p95 latency for short prompts, cost target <$0.0008/token, and SOC 2 evidence for procurement.
- Timeline: target pilot kickoff in Q4, production decision by end of Q1.

Primary asks:
1) Can you confirm the economic decision owner for this initiative? We need the person who signs off on budget/commitment (name & best email).
2) Procurement/legal path: will there be a formal RFP/SOW or do you use a standard PO + vendor questionnaire? Who on your side owns procurement?
3) Any compliance evidence we should surface first (SOC, logging/audit, data residency)?

What I can do next:
- Share a concise MAP template and a one-page pricing & commitment options. (attached: Redwood_MA_Planning_v1.xlsx, Redwood_MAPPricing_v3.pdf)
- Deliver a short SOC 2 + data handling summary and our standard SOW for procurement review.

Proposed next step: intro thread with the economic buyer + procurement lead so we can align the pilot scope and timing. If you prefer, I can send a short calendar invite for a 30-min alignment call next week.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra

From: Lina Ortega <lina.ortega@avatech.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: confirming decision owner & procurement path for Avatech

Hi Rishi — thanks for the clear recap and for the materials. Quick answers: 

1) Economic buyer is Michael Chen (CFO) — michael.chen@avatech.com. He owns capital allocation for AI/platform initiatives; he prefers to be looped in after we (product/eng) validate ROI assumptions, but is open to a short briefing.

2) Procurement process: we typically require a minimal SOW + PO for pilots under $50k. Any production/long-term contracts go through legal/procurement. Procurement lead is Jenna Park (jpark@avatech.com) — she handles vendor questionnaires and contracts.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II and an information security questionnaire are the usual asks. Data residency is US-only for now; we don't need an on-prem solution.

I'll introduce you to Michael on this thread and include Jenna. I'll also attach our vendor questionnaire (FYI). Can you please provide the short ROI slide and a one-page summary of the pilot scope and acceptance criteria so Michael sees concrete numbers?

Cheers,
Lina

Hi Michael — nice to e-meet you, and thanks Lina for the intro. Short note to respect your time:

Why this matters: Avatech's customer support use case maps cleanly to a cost/latency win with Redwood's runtime (we see 20–40% unit cost reduction vs. baseline approach for similar latency targets after modest batching & prefix caching).

Attachments sent with this message:
- One-page pilot scope + acceptance criteria (attached)
- Quick ROI slide (simple math: tokens/month -> estimated spend vs. current vendor)
- Suggested MAP workbook (we can tailor it live during a 30-min sync)

Asks for you:
- If you can confirm a budget envelope for a pilot (range is fine), that lets us size infra and present a low-risk pilot contract.
- If preferred, we can run a 20-minute briefing for finance/ops to show the ROI assumptions and contractual guarantees (SLA clauses we typically propose).

Proposed next step: 20-min call next Tue (Aug 25) to walk the ROI and pilot terms; I'll coordinate with Jenna on procurement items. If different timing works, tell me and we'll adjust.

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi / Lina — thanks for the summary and for looping me in. A few quick notes from finance: 

- Budget envelope: we can commit up to $40k for a timeboxed pilot if the acceptance criteria are clear and there is an explicit off-ramp at pilot end.
- Procurement: Jenna will review your SOW and vendor questionnaire. For pilots under $50k we do PO-based procurement; for anything above that we'll need a master services agreement.
- Risks: please include a short note on data handling and indemnity limits in the SOW; legal already flagged those as checklist items.

I'll join the ROI briefing if it is 20 minutes and focused on numbers. Tue Aug 25 11:00am PT works for me. Lina/Jenna — thanks for coordinating.

Michael Chen
Chief Financial Officer
Avatech
